subject: POC prompting playbook, evaluation metrics & acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Gupta <asha@novusai.com>, Miles Carter <miles.carter@novusai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC prompting playbook, evaluation metrics & acceptance criteria

Hi Asha / Miles — great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the POC moving toward a clear acceptance decision.

High-level success criteria (proposed):
- Quality: automated and human-eval quality score meets or exceeds your current baseline on the labeled subset (we'll propose concrete thresholds below).
- Safety & privacy: PII/sensitive output rate below 0.1% on sampled logs and any redaction gaps closed.
- Performance: p95 inference latency <350ms for typical 512-token interactions in your config.
- Operational: turnkey prompt ingestion + reproduceable eval report within 3 weeks of data receipt.

What we need from Novus to start ingestion and run the evals:
1) Prompt/log bundle (CSV or JSONL) with clear columns for: user_segment, prompt_text, expected_output (if available), timestamp. See attached prompt_template_v1.csv.
2) A labeled subset for quality checks (even 150–300 examples is helpful).
3) Any redaction rules we should apply before evaluation (PII fields, tokens to mask).
4) Point of contact and ownership for each item (data handoff owner + product reviewer).

Proposed timeline (flexible):
- Deliver logs (redacted) by Tue 2026-09-15
- Redwood ingests & baseline run by Fri 2026-09-17
- Quality + safety report by Thu 2026-09-24
- Joint review and demo week of 2026-09-28 (target 2026-09-30)

Owners:
- Novus: Asha (data owner) / Miles (product)
- Redwood: Jonas (engagement), Neha (eval lead), Marissa (solutions)

Attachments: [attachment: prompt_template_v1.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

Please confirm the timeline and whether you can provide a redacted log file by 9/15. Happy to adjust if you have constraints.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC prompting playbook, evaluation metrics & acceptance criteria

Thanks Jonas — helpful recap. We're aligned on the timeline in principle. Attaching a first export of our August prompt logs; this is a redacted extract (user IDs hashed) but let me know if you need additional fields.

Questions we have before ingestion: 
- For the labeled subset, are you OK with us providing labels as a separate CSV (format in the template)?
- On the quality threshold: what's a realistic baseline metric we should expect for an improvement? Our internal metric is "answer correctness" measured against human labels (we usually report F1 + EM).
- Can Redwood run the eval on hashed identifiers or do you require mapping to original IDs for cross-checks?

Attachments: [attachment: novus_prompt_logs_202608.csv (CSV, 1.8MB)]

Best,

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Gupta <asha@novusai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-11T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC prompting playbook, evaluation metrics & acceptance criteria

Hi Asha — thanks for the export, this looks good as an initial bundle. Quick answers + a concrete eval plan we can run once we have the files.

Short answers: 
- Labeled subset as a separate CSV works fine (please include the same prompt_id keys so we can join).
- We'll report both EM and F1 for correctness; realistic improvement targets depend on the existing model you use. For planning purposes, target +8–12% relative gain in F1 on the labeled slice would be a strong outcome for a model upgrade; we can calibrate after we see the baseline.
- Hashed IDs are OK for privacy; we only need stable keys to join logs to labels. If you can provide a mapping in a secure channel later that helps triage edge cases, that's optional.

Proposed evaluation plan (high level):
1) Ingest & validate schema (2 business days after receipt).
2) Data split: labeled subset (holdout for QA), automated metrics run on full bundle, human-eval on sampled failures (we'll flag ~200 borderline cases).
3) Metrics we will compute: EM, F1, response-safety (PII leakage rate), hallucination proxy (contradiction rate vs. expected_output), latency distribution (p50/p95).
4) Acceptance rules (draft):
   - EM >= baseline_EM + X (calibrate to baseline once ingested) OR F1 >= baseline_F1 + 8%
   - PII leakage <= 0.1% on sampled outputs
   - p95 latency <350ms in Redwood Dedicated config (we'll run on representative batch)
5) Deliverables: baseline report, per-segment breakdown, failure bucket examples, recommended prompt engineering changes and a short rollout plan.

Timeline (confirmed if you can deliver by 9/15):
- 9/15: Novus delivers redacted logs + labeled subset sample
- 9/17: Redwood ingestion complete + baseline run
- 9/24: Draft report delivered to Novus (includes metrics and failure examples)
- 9/30: Joint review + next-step decision meeting

We also attached a short draft POC SLA for review (POC_SLA_draft.docx) that covers data handling and retention.

If that looks good, Jonas and I will lock the timeline and kick off the ingestion once we receive the files.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
